name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,566

clue.text: Child captures cross subterranean beast

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a minor is a person under legal age
the tau cross is a T-shaped cross named after the Greek letter

explanation.surface: A youngster traps some angry monster that lives underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The tau cross is T-shaped, named after the Greek letter; 'subterranean' fits a beast kept in a maze below a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed monster of Greek myth lived in the Labyrinth beneath King Minos's palace on Crete.

clue.text: Independent governed nation

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent
to run a country is to govern it

explanation.surface: A self-ruling, autonomously governed country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Improvised cigar stuffed with pound of old vegetable

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so these letters are thrown together afresh
a thing stuffed with something has it packed inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L, from Latin libra, was the symbol for the pound in old British money

explanation.surface: A makeshift cigar is packed with a weight of some ancient vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old vegetable' looks like the definition, but 'of old' belongs with pound: L is the pre-decimal pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a bulb plant of the onion family, eaten and cooked as a pungent vegetable.

clue.text: Small-scale debtor?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who owes only a little money
setter's reading: one of Mary Norton's tiny people who live under the floorboards and take things from the humans above

explanation.walkthrough: The Borrowers is a children's novel by Mary Norton about miniature people, so a small-scale debtor is literally a very small person who borrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who takes a loan owes it back, so someone who borrows is a debtor; the tiny Norton characters make it small-scale.

clue.text: Normal tie rearranged to make room for single knockout game

indicators.note: rearranged means put into a different order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A regular draw gets reshuffled to fit in one more sudden-death match.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'normal tie' make room for one more letter, I, before all ten are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An eliminator is a qualifying contest or round in which the loser is knocked out of the competition.

clue.text: Wing headed by a 'W' when pronounced?

indicators.note: pronounced tells us to say the phrase out loud and listen for a word

blocks.note: in the alphabet the letter headed by W is X, so this is a letter X

explanation.surface: A building extension that starts with the letter W, if you say it out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Wing does begin with W, which is the trap; the letter that comes straight after W is X, and 'an X' said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or extension joined to a main one, as a wing of a house or hospital is.

clue.text: 80s car range

blocks.note: first meaning: the Ford family saloon sold in Britain from 1982
second meaning: a chain of jagged mountains, from the Spanish word for saw

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a range of cars from the 1980s; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford model was a common British company car, and the Spanish-derived word names a mountain chain.

clue.text: Aimless drawing of God in old comic

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters before it are set out in a silly new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless sketch of a deity appearing in some vintage comic book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old comic' reads like a magazine or a veteran comedian, but comic is the signal for the letters of 'God in old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to scribble absent-mindedly, producing idle sketches with no purpose or plan.

clue.text: Result of manufacturing deserting town: residents here hold power

blocks.note: cryptic meaning: when factories leave a town its shops close and the high street goes into decline, so it is a street going down
straight meaning: the London street where the Prime Minister and Chancellor live

explanation.surface: Deindustrialisation empties a town, and the people in charge live somewhere else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading of the name as a street that is downing, that is going down; the second is the real address.
explanation.definitionFit: Number 10 and Number 11 in this Westminster street are the official homes of the British Prime Minister and Chancellor.

clue.text: Plant in secluded place around running water

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a quiet corner is a tucked-away spot
a flow is a stream of moving water

explanation.surface: A flower grows in a quiet nook beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornflower is a blue-flowered annual that once grew wild among cereal crops.

clue.text: Proper athletics event

blocks.note: first meaning: fitting or suitable, an old-fashioned adjective
second meaning: a sporting gathering where races and competitions are held

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a 'proper' sports occasion; the archaic adjective sense, as in 'it is meet and right', is the one solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means suitable or fitting, and the noun is a track-and-field competition.

clue.text: Musician's revolutionary tune breaking sound barrier

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so this word is read backwards
to break into something is to get inside it

blocks.note: an air is a melody
Mach 1 is the speed of sound, written with the numeral as I

explanation.surface: A player's radical new melody smashes through the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed tune sits inside MACH I after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariachi is a member of a traditional Mexican street band of strings and trumpets.

clue.text: During resignation speech, cast out without finishing. That's unjust

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is never reached and is dropped

blocks.note: in a time is during it
what someone says when resigning
to oust is to expel

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out mid-resignation speech, before they can finish, which seems unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken words count as letters here: 'I quit' is the resignation speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquitous means grossly wicked or unfair, a stronger synonym for unjust.

clue.text: White bear on the run

blocks.note: wan means pale
a ted is a teddy bear

explanation.surface: A polar bear has escaped and is at large.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is sought by the police, as on a wanted poster for someone being hunted.

clue.text: Given new Punch, reading it over at random?

indicators.note: at random means in no fixed order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone handed a fresh copy of Punch magazine flicks through it haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British humour magazine; its capital letter disguises punch meaning energy or vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvigorate is to restore energy and vitality, which is to give something fresh punch.

clue.text: Defamed the Italian rider, opposed fixing

indicators.note: fixing something here means holding it fast inside

blocks.note: il is the Italian for the
a rider is a condition attached to something, as is an if
vied means competed against

explanation.surface: An Italian cyclist was slandered by rivals who resisted his race-fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rider looks like a cyclist, but here it is a proviso attached to a contract, the sense in which an if is a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To vilify is to speak or write about someone in an abusively disparaging way.

clue.text: Chuck fish food

blocks.note: to chuck away is to dump
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Throw out the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is a small boiled or steamed ball of dough, eaten in stews or filled.

clue.text: Physical instruction book

blocks.note: first meaning: done with the hands, as in hands-on labour
second meaning: a handbook explaining how to operate something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fitness guide; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual labour is bodily work with the hands, and a handbook of operating directions is also so called.

clue.text: Heartless scavenging animal returning cry of pain without care

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out
returning means going back the way it came, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: the hyena is a carrion-eating African mammal
ow is what someone yells when hurt

explanation.surface: A hyena, missing its heart, comes back yowling in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carelessly is doing it any old how, in a haphazard and sloppy manner.

clue.text: Unconsummated threesome breaks rules

indicators.note: never consummated means never completed, so the final letter is missing
to break something is to smash it into pieces that can be put back differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A three-way liaison that was never completed violates the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks rules' reads as one phrase, but breaks is the signal and rules alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorems are mathematical propositions proved from axioms, general principles or laws in a loose sense.

clue.text: Doubles player, with back gone, retires, giving set up

indicators.note: with its back gone means the final letter has been taken off
to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: in doubles tennis each player has a partner

explanation.surface: A tennis doubles player with a bad back quits, leaving the match arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone up is to frame or trap them, tricking them into an incriminating position.

clue.text: See why esteem, mostly, is said to spell growth

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
said tells us these words are spoken, and the sounds spell letter names

blocks.note: said aloud it is the name of a letter
said aloud it is the name of a letter
said aloud it runs through three letter names

explanation.surface: A puzzled plea to understand why respect is supposed to lead to growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is heard as letter names: see, why, and es-tee-em, which loses its last sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal sac of fluid or tissue that forms in the body, a kind of lump.

clue.text: Bolt joined with pins and needles temporarily

blocks.note: to bolt is to run away
pins and needles is a prickling, tingly feeling

explanation.surface: A bolt fastened with pins and needles holds only for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt and pins and needles look like hardware, but bolt is a verb and pins and needles is the prickling feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting lasts only a brief moment, so doing it fleetingly means for a short while.

clue.text: Blues lady sung like a siren?

indicators.note: something sung is voiced aloud, so we listen to the sound

blocks.note: the two-tone wail of a British emergency siren is imitated as nee-nah

explanation.surface: A blues singer whose voice is compared to a seductive siren of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The siren of myth is the false path; it is the police or ambulance kind, whose noise children imitate as nee-nah.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina Simone was an American singer celebrated for blues, jazz and soul recordings.

clue.text: Bandido-cum-entertainer conceals record

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep something out of sight within, so the letters lie inside these words

blocks.note: found running across the joined words

explanation.surface: An outlaw who doubles as a performer is hiding the records.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is an official written or printed paper that serves as a record of something.

clue.text: Blind gaping, scratching head

indicators.note: to scratch out the head is to strike off the first letter

blocks.note: a yawning gap is a gaping one

explanation.surface: A blind person, mouth hanging open, scratches their head.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind looks like an adjective about sight, but it is the noun for a window shade.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a window or shopfront to keep out sun, like a shade.
